parts:
Before I change anything, here is what I found, because one of the findings changes how this can work.

**What smooth-poincare-4d already has.** The capture tools were ported on 21 November and all 117 tool tests pass on your Mac. Codex capture is working: three Codex chats are registered under `papers/investigations-1/01_chiral_metric_evolution/chat-histories/`.

**What it lacks compared with shifted-zeta-positivity.** Everything on the Claude side: there are no `chat-histories/claude-cowork/` registries, and no Claude conversation is recorded (yesterday's manuscript-review session included). It also has no `.codex/hooks.json`.

**The problem.** In shifted-zeta-positivity each Claude session recorded itself every turn by reading its own transcript file in the cloud workspace (`~/.claude/projects/…jsonl`) with `record_Claude_cowork_chat.py`. That file no longer exists in Cowork sessions. I searched this session's whole workspace and checked what the runtime has open: there is no transcript on disk, so `spool` and `capture` have nothing to read. The October procedure cannot run as written, here or in any later session on this runtime.

**What is left.** The session's event log on claude.ai is still complete, and `record_Claude_export_chat.py cowork` was built to convert it (it is how the early RH sessions were recovered). It has to be read from a browser signed in to claude.ai, through an internal endpoint that nobody has re-tested since October. Failing that, the only option is the kind of clearly labelled, unregistered partial record the Codex setup chats left on 21 November.

I have three questions for you about scope and how to get the text.

parts:
Scope: smooth-poincare-4d already has working Codex capture (3 Codex chats registered). Compared with shifted-zeta-positivity it lacks everything for Claude sessions (no chat-histories/claude-cowork registries, no Claude chat recorded) and the Codex hook file (.codex/hooks.json). Which should I set up?
- Claude sessions (Recommended) — Create the claude-cowork registries and READMEs, document the Claude procedure in tools/CHAT_HISTORY.md and AGENTS.md, and record this conversation as the first entry. Codex files are left alone.
- Claude + Codex hooks — The above, plus a .codex/hooks.json adapted from shifted-zeta-positivity. You would still need to review and trust the hooks once in Codex before they run.
- Codex hooks only — Only add .codex/hooks.json. Claude sessions stay unrecorded.
Source: Cowork sessions no longer keep the transcript file that the October per-turn capture read, so that procedure cannot run. The remaining authentic source is this session's event log on claude.ai, read from a signed-in browser (what tools/record_Claude_export_chat.py converts). How should I get this conversation's text?
- I read it in the browser — I use the browser on your Mac to read this session's event log from claude.ai, keep only the public messages, and register them. You must be signed in to claude.ai there and may get a site-approval prompt. If the browser refuses claude.ai or the endpoint has changed, I fall back to preparing a script for you.
- You run a script — I stay out of your browser. I prepare a paste-in console script and the exact command; you run them when you want a capture. I cannot test the endpoint beforehand.
- Partial record only — No browser at all. I save a clearly labelled, unregistered partial record of this chat's visible text, as the Codex setup chats did on 21 November, and document that authentic Claude capture is unavailable for now.
Later chats: shifted-zeta-positivity's AGENTS.md gives a standing authorization: sessions capture and refresh their own chat without asking each time. Should smooth-poincare-4d say the same for later Claude sessions?
- Capture without asking — Same as the reference: each Claude session records itself once its destination is clear and refreshes at the end of every turn, by whichever source works; if none does, it leaves a labelled partial record.
- Only when I ask — No standing rule. A Claude session captures its chat only when you tell it to, for example 'capture this chat'.

Sign-in: The Claude app's built-in browser is not signed in to claude.ai (it shows the login page), and no Chrome with the Claude extension is connected, so I cannot read this session's event log yet. Can you sign in there? Press Cmd+Shift+B in the Claude desktop app to show the Browser pane, sign in to claude.ai, then pick the first option.
- Done, I'm signed in — I continue: test the event-log endpoint, then capture this chat. The sign-in stays in the app's browser profile, which is also what lets later Claude sessions capture themselves; you can sign out there at any time.
- Prepare a script instead — Don't use the built-in browser. I write a console script and the commands for you to run in your own browser when you want a capture. I cannot test the endpoint first.
- Partial record only — No browser. I set up the registries and documentation, and save a clearly labelled, unregistered partial record of this chat's visible text.

metadata.rendering: progress update between tool calls as the event log records it (flagged there as narration): a condensed rewrite of what the assistant wrote, kept by the runtime for display, not the assistant's verbatim wording

archive_metadata.format: ChatGPT-style conversation mapping; local conversion, not an official provider export
archive_metadata.source_kind: Claude Cowork cloud session event log (claude.ai GET /v1/code/sessions/{id}/events), read in the signed-in browser, reduced there to completed public messages and transferred with a SHA-256 check
archive_metadata.message_timestamps: Event times, in seconds since Unix epoch and ISO 8601: the session's own timestamp where the event carries one, otherwise the server's event time (typed messages); the conversation create_time is the creation time in the session object on claude.ai
archive_metadata.coverage: Messages typed by the person (including any sent while a reply was in progress, with the names of files sent with them) and interruption markers; the options the person selected in question cards; the text ending each completed turn (phase final_answer); and, as phase commentary, progress updates between tool calls in the condensed form the event log holds (not the assistant's verbatim wording), question cards rendered as text, and notes and file-card captions sent through tools; recorded through the event log as read. A reply still in progress at a read enters with the next one
omitted_record_types: system, developer and harness text (reminders, date notes, memory snapshots, continuation summaries, hook feedback, skill text, local command output)
tool calls and outputs, except the chat-visible items named in coverage
permission prompts, control and environment events, usage and cost figures
attachment contents (file names are kept in message metadata)

session.title_source: the title in the session object on claude.ai

project.name: Smooth Poincare Conjecture 4d
project.name_source: stated to ingest by the capturing session
project.uuid_source: stated to ingest and equal to the decoded chat_project_id

session.identity_check: the log names the SDK session id e587c35b-d7ff-5def-b63b-ddfffe9f9e48 that the capturing session read from its own workspace

source_events.read_by: the reader of tools/record_Claude_browser_chat.py, run in a browser signed in to claude.ai
source_events.note: The store holds the public records of every read of this session's event log, outside the repository; sha256_of_events_json is the SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(events sorted by sequence_num) computed in the browser at the last read. Neither the event log nor the store is kept in the repository
source_events.reduction: public records only; the reader drops every other event in the page

archive_metadata.delivered_files_note: Paths reported by device_commit_files, names of file cards, and files the capturing session named to ingest with --delivered; other files written by shell commands or saved as project documents are not detected
